The '''Red Desert''', also known as the Olotono Desert, is the largest desert in [[New Ayre]] and is the ______ -largest desert in the world by area, occupying approxly 2,622,500 square kilometres (1,629,545 mi2). It is located primarily in [[Andsaudare]] and is bounded by the[[Fedaea Mountains]], to its south and west, and the [[Demeeri]] to its north. To the north, the desert grades into the [[Padeshi Savanna]] and the [[Hinitru basin]]. The central parts of the desert are filled with sand dunes, some of which are 300 metres (980 ft) high and span 32 kilometres (20 mi) long, are the third-largest in the world. The southern parts of the desert have gravel plains and scattered mountain outcrops. 

Inhabited by hunter-gatherers since Pre-Tavalan times, the desert faced migration in the 19th century of [[Taval|Alqiran]], [[Hazia|Iainoan]], and many [[Ethnic Groups of Ayuma|Ayuman peoples]], transforming it from a conflictive borderland zone to an integral part of [[Andsaudare]], though it is still one of the most sparsely populated places on andah.
==Entomology==
Olotono is one of the historical names used for the modern desert. It is also natively by the [[Iainoa|Iainoan]]peoples as referred to as Olotono Slai (lit. 'Red Desert'). The region forms the central portion of [[New Ayre]] and borders most nations in the mainland continent. It also includes another region to the north known as [[Peiay]].
==Geography==
The Olotono Region, the largest region in Andsaudare is around ________ square kilometres ( ______ sq mi), and borders [[Prstreula]], [[Ohtina]], [[United Delet]], [[Umarcia]], and [[Iainoa]]. There is only one significant settlement in the desert: [[Tarnava]]

The Olotono is a plateau, with an elevation above sea level that ranges from 1,500 metres in the south, falling to about 500 metres along the northern limits and the. The areas with altitudes between 1,400 and 1,600 metres are characterised as arid, receiving as much as 40–50 millimetres of rainfall annually. More typical of the Olotono is an average annual rainfall of 250 millimetres or less. The landscape consists of sparse shrubland, sand dune and bare hills. In more recent years, the Olotono has suffered from increasingly erratic rainfall patterns, which have led to an increasing frequency of major droughts: in 1744–1745; 1746; and most recently in 1758–1559, during which pastoralists claim to have lost 70–90 percent of their cattle. It also includes another region in the north known as [[Peiay]].
==Climate==
The Olotono has less than 10 mm (0.39 in) of rain annually and is almost completely barren. Besides rain being scarce, it is also unpredictable. Central Olotono gets less rain (5 mm) than northern Olotono (160 mm). This is due to several factors. Winds coming from the Eanif's Ocean lose part of their humidity when passing the [[Fedaea Mountains]], and are essentially dry when they reach the desert. On the other hand, winds coming from the [[Rianan Ocean]] are pressed down by hot air from the west; 

The dry climate of Olotono reflects the almost complete lack of bodies of water on the surface. Most rivers flow underground and/or are dry for most of the year. Even when they are not, they usually drain into endorheic basins, without reaching the sea. 
==Plants and animals==
===Flora===
Several unusual species of plants and animals are found in this desert, many of which are endemic and highly adapted to the specific climate of the area.

One of the most well-known endemic plants of the Olotono is the Eitchk plant, a shrub-like plant that grows two long, strap-shaped leaves continuously throughout its lifetime. These leaves may be several meters long, gnarled, and twisted from the desert winds. The taproot of the plant develops into a flat, concave disc with age. Eitchk is notable for its survival in the extremely arid central Olotono conditions, made possible by its ability to capture moisture from fogs.
